finding: The intended ordering is to request owned-tree termination when stop is selected, then confirm required cleanup under one shared budget. Current cleanup can do work before that termination request.

paths.detail: For an active or unknown Job, begin_job_cleanup calls the member-capture closure before the owned TerminateJobObject closure. Capture performs width-dependent enumeration and opens. Its shared software deadline does not prevent that work from delaying the first termination request.

The supervisor calls D::close before teardown. In extendable mode, Extension::close locks the shared state mutex. This can wait for other state work before termination. Fixed mode does not take this extension lock.

unresolved_objections: Preserve prompt first termination of an active or unknown owned tree on timeout, owner exit and normal root exit without post-stop member-discovery delay.
Keep extension stop linearization off the blocking shared-state mutex while resolving concurrent grants.
Prove required original-process settlement without substituting Job accounting or best-effort messages for missing original handles.

preserved_evidence.interpretation: Their recorded focused test outcomes remain unchanged. They do not establish the newly reviewed first-termination ordering contract or general descendant settlement.

reference_disposition: The retained repaired reference remains ineligible after G28. Porting the current pre-kill census alone would not resolve this ordering objection.
limits: This is a source-ordering and readiness finding, not a new empirical delayed-kill measurement.
No accepted replacement implementation or new speed result follows from this finding.
The intended protection and deadline requirements are retained. No benchmark acceptance rule or expected result is relaxed.
